item.title: Issue #2820 created
item.description:
Ambiguity caused by introducing `OccurrenceIndicator` after `CastTarget`

Today's merging of #2777 brought this change of the XQuery 4.0 grammar:

676,677c676,677
<          ::= CastExpr ( 'castable' 'as' CastTarget '?'? )?
< CastExpr ::= PipelineExpr ( 'cast' 'as' CastTarget '?'? )?
---
>          ::= CastExpr ( 'castable' 'as' CastTarget OccurrenceIndicator? )?
> CastExpr ::= PipelineExpr ( 'cast' 'as' CastTarget OccurrenceIndicator? )?
1177a1178,1180
>            | TypedArrayType
>            | TypedMapType
>            | TypedRecordType

This now uses OccurrenceIndicator? after CastTarget:

CastableExpr ::= CastExpr ( "castable" "as" CastTarget OccurrenceIndicator? )?
CastExpr     ::= PipelineExpr ( "cast" "as" CastTarget OccurrenceIndicator? )?
CastTarget   ::= TypeName
               | ChoiceItemType
               | EnumerationType
               | TypedArrayType
               | TypedMapType
               | TypedRecordType
OccurrenceIndicator ::= "?" | "*" | "+"

This introduces an ambiguity with addition and multiplication operators. For example:

4 cast as xs:integer + -5

can be read as either:

(4 cast as xs:integer+) - 5

or:

(4 cast as xs:integer) + (-5)

Similarly, * after a cast target can be read either as an occurrence indicator or as a multiplication operator.

The spec has the extra-grammatical constraint xgc: occurrence-indicators, but its wording appears to apply only to SequenceType:

Any occurrence of "+", "?" or "*", that follows a sequence type is assumed to be an occurrence indicator, which binds to the last ItemType in the SequenceType.

Here, however, the relevant grammar uses CastTarget, not SequenceType, so it is unclear whether this disambiguation rule is intended to apply.

This causes LALR(2) parser generation conflicts for the new grammar. The old grammar used only '?'? after CastTarget, which did not create the same conflict.

If the intent is to apply xgc: occurrence-indicators here as well, then expressions such as:

4 cast as xs:integer + 5

would become syntactically invalid for the same reason as the existing treat as item() + 5 example: the + would be consumed as an occurrence indicator, and parentheses would be required to force addition. This would affect these test cases, then resulting in syntax errors:

  • op-numeric-add-13
  • op-numeric-add-14
  • op-numeric-add-15
  • op-numeric-add-16

These test cases, expecting syntax errors, would parse OK, so they need to be adapted to the changes of #2777:

  • K-SeqExprCastable-1
  • K-SeqExprCastable-2
  • K-SeqExprCastable-3
  • K-SeqExprCastable-4a
  • K-SeqExprCastable-12a
  • K-SeqExprCast-1
  • K-SeqExprCast-2
  • K-SeqExprCast-3a

One final remark: rather than repeating the optional OccurrenceIndicator in CastableExpr and CastExpr, it could also be made part of CastTarget.
